sections.h2: Five landlocked states burn 28.0 bcm, 8.3% of EU gas use, and have no port

chart.title: Even the largest landlocked consumer, Hungary, burns far less gas than Germany
chart.source: Eurostat 2024 balances, as charted in the original post.

sections.means: Their gas arrives only after crossing at least one border and paying at least one tariff, so their position depends on their neighbours' systems.
sections.todo: Plan landlocked supply around the neighbouring systems and tariffs it must cross, since no cargo can be landed directly.

sections.h2: Russian pipeline gas fell from more than 40% of EU imports in 2021 to roughly 11% in 2024

chart.title: Russia's share of EU pipeline gas imports shrank as the pipes themselves closed
chart.sub: Russia's share of EU pipeline gas imports, %.

sections.means: Some of the fall was policy, but a material part was that the pipes stopped existing.
sections.todo: Treat the remaining routes as scarce and expect importers to compete for the same LNG cargoes.

sections.h2: The EU ban ends Russian LNG on 31 December 2026 and pipeline gas on 30 September 2027

chart.title: Two closures came first, and the legal ban now fixes the last two dates
events: Underwater blasts rupture three of the four Nord Stream pipelines
Russian gas stops crossing Ukraine; TurkStream is the only Russian pipeline into the EU
Council approves the stepwise ban by qualified majority, 24 to 2

sections.means: The deadline was set by qualified majority, so Hungary and Slovakia hold no veto over it.
sections.todo: Hungary and Slovakia should plan for the September 2027 pipeline deadline rather than rely on a court challenge.

sections.h2: Austrian and Slovak transit tariffs are rising by roughly 79% to 331%

chart.title: Tariffs jump most where transit gas once flowed: Austria-Italy up about 331%
chart.sub: Reported or proposed tariff increases, roughly, %.

sections.means: Fixed network costs are recovered over less gas, so higher tariffs push shippers to other routes and throughput falls again.
sections.todo: Shippers should compare the northern route via Poland or Lithuania against the Austrian and Slovak corridor on cost.
